# Public-demo local acceptance run

**Date:** 2026-09-25
**Environment:** Windows 11, Docker Desktop, local mode (no VPS, no domain, no TLS certificate authority — a self-signed cert generated by `scripts/public_demo_cert.sh`)

## Composition and startup

```powershell
py -3.12 scripts/public_demo_env.py        # generates deploy/public-demo/.env with fresh random secrets
bash scripts/public_demo_cert.sh           # generates deploy/public-demo/certs/tls.{crt,key}
bash scripts/public_demo.sh up -d --build
```

All 11 long-running services (nginx, frontend, rag-gateway, worker, redis, egress-proxy, metabase, metabase-db, analytics-db, airflow, airflow-db) reported `healthy` within 80 seconds of a cold `up`.

## Edge exposure (port scan)

```
port 80: OPEN     (nginx, redirects to 443)
port 443: OPEN    (nginx)
port 6379: closed (redis; bound to a Docker-internal network only)
port 5432: closed (postgres instances)
port 8080: closed (airflow; not published)
```

Only nginx's two ports are reachable from the host. Every other service (redis, both Postgres instances, Metabase, Airflow, the RAG gateway, the worker) has no published port.

## Host boundary (static policy)

```powershell
python scripts/check_public_demo_policy.py                 # local mode
python scripts/check_public_demo_policy.py --strict-release
```

Local mode: `PASS (13 services)`. No privileged mode, host networking, PID/IPC namespace, Docker-socket mount, unlisted host-path bind, root user, or missing `cap_drop`/`no-new-privileges`/read-only root/memory limit/restart policy/health check.

Strict-release mode (first pass, before the GHCR publish below): `FAIL` on the four services that were still local builds (`airflow`, `frontend`, `worker`, `rag-gateway`) because they lacked a registry digest. After the GHCR publish, only `airflow` still fails strict-release — see the update at the end of this file.

## Egress isolation

Tested from the one-shot `check` service (`--profile checks`), which sits on the `app` and `egress` networks with no outbound route of its own:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Direct request to `example.com`, no proxy | `000` (unreachable — no route) |
| Through `egress-proxy`, to the allowlisted `example.com` | `200` |
| Through `egress-proxy`, to non-allowlisted `google.com` | `403` |
| Through `egress-proxy`, to `169.254.169.254` (cloud metadata) | `403` |

From inside the `worker` container directly (Python `socket.create_connection`): a connection to `8.8.8.8:53` and to `169.254.169.254:80` both raised `OSError: [Errno 101] Network is unreachable` — the container has no outbound route at all; only `egress-proxy` does, and only to its allowlist.

## Metabase

```powershell
$env:ANALYTICS_SOURCE = "release"   # already the versions.env default
bash scripts/public_demo_load_release.py --release-dir <extracted lucasrangelss/brazil-education-data-lake v1>
bash scripts/public_demo.sh up -d
bash scripts/public_demo.sh --profile seed run --rm metabase-seed
```

The loader verified the release manifest (SHA-256 `44f259602a688432dddbae6b0306a6957514a634d57d94a0abd3cff30f4b3506`) and wrote a 27,830-row CSV derivative plus its own hash record; the analytics-db init script re-checked that CSV hash against the record before loading, so an edited derivative would refuse to load. The seed script created one Postgres role restricted to the `approved` schema, one view, two non-SQL cards, one dashboard, and enabled its public link, printing UUID `c03e83ba-15e2-4daf-a9b6-3788a65fb00e`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /public/dashboard/<approved uuid>` | `200` |
| `GET /public/dashboard/<a stale, previously-approved uuid>` | `404` (nginx location is hardcoded to the current UUID; a rotated UUID needs `nginx` recreated, not just restarted — see the runbook) |
| `GET /admin`, `/question`, `/api/database`, `/api/card`, ... | `403` (blocked at nginx, never reaches Metabase) |
| Dashboard description | Correctly states the real source once loaded: *"Public FNDE SIOPE / IBGE derivative from the lucasrangelss/brazil-education-data-lake Kaggle release, hash-verified before load. Declared values, not audited."* |

**Bug found and fixed in this run:** the seed script originally hardcoded the dashboard description to "Synthetic fixture data" regardless of `ANALYTICS_SOURCE`. It now reads `ANALYTICS_SOURCE` at seed time and states the real source. Do not reintroduce a fixed label.

## Airflow

```powershell
docker exec public-demo-airflow-1 airflow dags list
```

Both mounted DAGs load with no import errors and report `is_paused = True`:

```
education_monitoring_demo      | is_paused: True
education_siope_annual_update  | is_paused: True
```

`brazil-public-data-map`'s `pncp_incremental_update.py` (schedule `0 */6 * * *`, no `is_paused_upon_creation`) is deliberately not mounted — see the Dockerfile comment in `deploy/public-demo/airflow/Dockerfile`. The Airflow webserver has no nginx route (`GET /airflow` on the public edge returns `404`) and port 8080 is not published; only an operator with `docker exec` can reach it.

## Recovery

```powershell
docker restart public-demo-rag-gateway-1
```

Restarting a public application container returns it to `healthy` without host intervention (health check passes within its configured `start_period`); it holds no state of its own (Redis is the state store), so nothing is lost by a restart.

## Not run in this pass

- The multi-cluster / VPS profile: out of scope until a provider, domain, and management-access method are supplied (spec section 14.2).
- A load test against the public-demo profile specifically (the Compose-only benchmark in `docs/evidence/compose-benchmark-2026-09-24.md` used the plain two-worker profile, not this hardened one).

## Update: real GHCR images (same day, later run)

Both `ai-platform-rag-observability` (tag `0.2.1`) and this repo (tag `v0.2.0`) publish an immutable image to GHCR on a signed tag as of this run (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `release` job). `versions.env` now pins both by tag+digest instead of a local build; only `airflow` remains a local build (its Dockerfile bakes in DAGs fetched from two other repos at pinned commits, not published as its own image).

```powershell
python scripts/public_demo_env.py
python scripts/public_demo_env.py --set EDUCATION_RELEASE_DIR=./data/education-release
# copy an extracted lucasrangelss/brazil-education-data-lake v1 into deploy/public-demo/data/education-release/
bash scripts/public_demo.sh up -d --build
curl -sk -X POST https://localhost/v1/answer -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"question":"What was the population of Acrelandia in 2023?"}'
```

The real `rag-gateway` image, pulled from GHCR by digest, answered correctly through the hardened nginx edge: *"In 2023, Acrelândia had a population of 13,353. [municipality-1200013#c004]"*, with a citation carrying the dataset slug, version, and manifest hash. `python scripts/check_public_demo_policy.py --strict-release` reports exactly one finding (`airflow`, expected). The fixture stand-in (`runtime_lab/rag_fixture.py`) is no longer used by this profile; it remains in the repo only as a documented, independently tested reference for the API contract.
